scenarios.title: Delete a referenced document graph once
plannedActions: Complete original typed-graph integrity checks and valid metadata edit. Acquire the scene lease and capture current snapshot plus complete two-event history; require five live edit leases.
Submit character-only deletion using current version and lease. Require exact 409/item_in_use, identical nonlease snapshot and complete event response.
Reuse the refused command ID for scene, character, image, entry and cue deletions in parent-first order with current versions, leases and timing version.
Require one successful receipt, one sequence/timing increment, five versioned tombstones and an empty live snapshot that is still not importable.
Read full events and require the two old records unchanged plus one exact five-change command event with complete before/after values, actor, label and real request-time bounds.
Replay the identical successful payload. Require identical receipt and unchanged nonlease snapshot/history, no new event or version/counter movement, empty R2, 80 HTTP checks and zero outbound.
expectedOutcomes: With current public versions and live edit leases, deleting the referenced character alone returns exact 409/item_in_use. A fresh public snapshot excluding the time-sensitive leases field and the complete event response are unchanged. The same refused command ID is then reused with a repaired all-five-item delete payload and succeeds, showing that the refused attempt did not block this corrected retry. No internal receipt/index read or storage failure injection is performed.

One command deletes scene, character, image, entry and cue, deliberately placing parents before their dependants. The successful receipt contains exactly those five prior items in operation order, each incremented once and marked deleted, at sequence three, epoch one and timing version two. Public snapshot has no live items, five exact metadata-only tombstones with empty data, canImport false and unchanged other nonlease fields. One new event preserves each complete before/after item, actor, command ID, label and request-bounded timestamp; the two original events remain exact.

An exact replay of the successful corrected payload by the same actor returns the identical original receipt. Fresh snapshot excluding leases and the full event response remain identical to the post-delete state, with no additional sequence, timing, item-version or event change. R2 stays empty and outbound attempts remain zero. This is sequential public-state/idempotency evidence, not restart durability, hidden-store nonmutation, permanent erasure, arbitrary race or fault safety.

associations.rationale: Character-only delete is refused by the aggregate reference guard; the complete parent-first graph delete succeeds when all dependants are deleted in the same command. Individual scene/image refusal branches are not newly isolated.
associations.uncertainty: Independent semantic review required. Sequential owned service HTTP and public state only; no internal receipt/index reads, forced failure/race, restart/crash, permanent erasure, live provider or native behavior. Mapping is not measured execution.
